[i][b]Official Statement from the Government of the OER[/b]

The Oceanic Enclave Republic officially declares the immediate imposition of sanctions against the Sanguinian Democratic Republic and the Socialist Republic of Qianxun. Effective immediately, all trade routes across the Argos Ocean and Archal Ocean are closed to the regimes.

This has been made for defending peace, stability, and the values of democracy against the expanding threats posed by socialist and communist aggression. In coordination with our allies within the EDU, the Oceanic Enclave Republic is willing to suspend all trade, financial relations, and investment activity with both the Sanguinian Democratic Republic and the Socialist Republic of Qianxun.

Enforce strict naval and aerial blockades to prevent any cargo or commercial activity from reaching or passing through the Argos and Archal Oceans. Coordinate intelligence sharing and enforcement measures with EDU partners to ensure the effectiveness of these sanctions.

[u]Statement from President Ironvisak Willham[/u]

"The Oceanic Enclave Republic will never allow hostile socialist and communist regimes to undermine the liberty and prosperity of free nations. These sanctions and trade blockades are not acts of aggression, they are measures of defense, designed to protect our people, our allies, and the stability of the global order. We stand united with our partners in the EDU, resolute in our belief that peace is preserved through strength and vigilance. The enemies of freedom will find no safe passage through our oceans, no access to our markets, and no influence over our democratic way of life.

Our message is clear. we will defend our sovereignty, we will defend our allies, and we will defend democracy itself."[/u][/i]

[spoiler=New information and a change of plans]
[b][u]Supricing new information in the battle for the two lower islands[/u][/b]
Nordiheim command was rather baffeled by the new information that would quickly come in after their airforce had engaged the hostile aircraft in the lower islands airspace, the various surveilance, aswell as the advanced systems of the stealth fighters, had managed to atain a positive identification of who the aircraft belonged to.
The [b]PDF[/b], the military of Pantagruel itself, this made it easier to piece together who this unknown force, who went under the markings of [b]UDF[/b], actualy might be, the conclusion with the most agreement was that it most likely was the Amaralo People's Army, but why were they using a new insignia and doing joint military attacks with pantagruel that was so blatent and easy to see, had all pretence been thrown out the window?
Why were they doing someting this rash, had someting changed?

The minister of war, Grand general Thormod Thormodson III, saw someting ells tough, justification for their latest actions and a transformation of what it could be labbeled as.
Now they could claim that they were simply doing a intervention to defend another nation, who were within their sphere of influence, from a direct attack from a foreign nation and their litteral puppet trying to directly take advantage of a nation embroiled in a civil war.
With the local people on the island even asking Nordiheim for help to defend itself, ofcorse they had acted!
It also provided evidence to support the reports of Pantagruels attack and hostile takeover of the Amaralo People's Army earlier in the civil war and basicly stripped them of any pretence of that faction still being anyting other then under Pantagruels controll.

Thormod wasted no time ordering changes to the curent plans and orders of the Nordiheimian military;
>The invasion fleet were now to be crushed with the large fleet to its east and the assets to its west to converg on it and desimate it with the use of anti-ship missiles and torpedoes, it were to be gone imidiatly!
>The secound fleet with the COMINT ship were to no longer hold its possition and wait for the Armed Restoration Fronts action ageinst it, they would move out of their main shiping lane and towards the waters of Italian duch in the west/north-west and secure the shiping lanes there.
There was a chance that the Junta would use this suden move in their propaganda to proclaim that them joust "baring their teeth" had made a potential enemy flee from them to bolster moral and suport with their people, but this was someting they would joust have to take in stride as there was bigger fish to pay attention to right now.
It would also mean that they would need to be a bit more carefull with the supply ships going to the Argossians on Mainland Astanir, but any shortfall could most likely be covered by air on the airfields that was being expanded and improved in the Argossian tribal areas.
>There would be declared a "no fly zone" over and around the two lower islands to "protect" them from foreign attacks, the Pantagruel airforce would be faced with the warning that if they did not turn around they would be shot down.
>And lastly, gatter up a elite team to search for wreckage to use as aditional evidence, there were no way that none of the aircraft from Pantagruel was shot down by the stealth fighters and those aircraft pieces could be usefull to have as proof.

To help support Nordiheims "claims" of "aiding a nation in need ageinst another nation" the Nordiheim foreign office would get to work with what they allready had to make a solid case.
Both the reports of the blatant hostile takeover of the Amaralo People's Army by Pantagruel and the more direct proof, that was gathered by their different surveilance systems, that showed them in a joint attack ageinst the people of Astanirs lower islands would be used.
Any evidence of brutality provided by agents on the islands would also be used if it could be found.

[b][u]Destroying the invasion[/u][/b]

From both east and west forces from Nordiheim would converge on the invading fleet, when they got in range a large barage of anti-ship missiles would be fired from both directions to overwelm the AA defences of the ships and turn them into sinking wrecks.
In the sky both the stealth fighters and regular fighters would clear the sky of any remaining targets together with the AA systems that was being suplied to the local Argossians as fast as could be done, the large SHH1-1C Sky Leviatan would allow some of the smaller systems to be delivered ready for immidiate use.

Ones these two tasks were done the large fleet would take up position to help enforce the "no fly zone" together with the stealth fighters and other assets, any Pantagruel aircraft that would aproche would be given the ultimatum "If you enter this no fly zone you will be fired upon!".
Meanwhile high presicion missile and air strikes would be conducted on the invading forces that had landed on the islands using a combination of the local Argossians, Nordiheims agents and stealth UAVs that was monitoring the islands, any significant gattering of their forces would be targeted aswell as any rally point that was identified.
A EWJ-2 Curlew Electronic warfare airplane would also be called to the islands with a escort to disable the invaders ability to comunicate and organize themself.

One command were given tough, those of the UDF that laid down their weapons and surendered would be taken in and treated propperly according to the propper laws and regulations.
This would also be comunicated to the Argossian militias together with the explanation that it would help give their cause in the eyes of the world but also the other people of Astanir, someting that could be very beneficial to them.

[b][u]Mainland Astanir[/u][/b]

While tings were spicy over in the south-east there was also tings going on over in mainland Astanir.
With the Sui-mana being able to attend negotiations with representation physicaly present tings could hopefully continue going forward, but the Argossian tribes would also have to be told about the invasion.
The Nordiheimian diplomats there would inform them in full about what had happened and was going on over at the lower islands, with Pantagruel atempting an invasion together with their puppet faction and their vichious attacks on their fellow Argossians there.
This would also bring up a question, what was the situation of the representatives they sendt to Pentagruel?
Had they heard anyting back from them, or could they even comunicate with them at all?

They also cautioned them that the supply lines to them were not the most stable right now and as such some caution would be adviced, in adition the usualy very detailed military inteligence that they were being given would be slightly less so until more surveilance could be aranged trough such means as creating better airfields.

[b][u]The warning to the Sui-Mana Enclave[/u][/b]

The agents in and around the Sui-Mana enclave had reported back military movements that the Sui-mana had executed wich gave the Nordiheimian some cause of worry, spesificaly their recent classes with the Democratic Army of Astanir.
The front that they now were geting with them could potentialy endanger the enclave with the problem of having active and strong lines of engagements in all directions, with the added danger of attacks on the Democratic faction, if they even was that anymore, being incentiviced to do a large atack on them.
While they were somewhat busy right now it did not seem that it would last long, as such a change in the Sui-mana actions would need to happen to make them seem like less of a problem.

Nordiheim would comunicate this increasing danger to the Sui-mana leadership and point out that if they got targeted by both the Democratic and National forces they would undouptably be crushed and there would be rather little that they could do about it no matter how much weapons and supplies they airdropped to them.
As such they were heavely adviced to disengage from the Democratic forces and move out of their territory and back into their own, there they would be helped by the Nordiheimian agents to sett up defensive possitions and lines using the mines they had been given to make minefields  in an effort to make themselfs an uninviting target.
Hopefully the Democratic forces would see the Astaniran National Forces as a bether and more inviting target to attack instead.

If the Sui-mana needed a target to attack they should go for the National forces to, more spesificaly in the north-vestern direction as this would potentialy bring them closer to their fellow Argossian brothers and sisters, wich could eventualy create the opportunity to join the territories together as one and eliminate perhaps their greatest challenge to achive their goal.

Now the Nordiheimian would have to wait and hope that they had erned enough trust and good will with the Sui-mana and the other Argossians for them to listen to their advice and counceling.[/spoiler]

[quote=qianxun;60425545][b]You have nothing to lose but your chains.[/b]

Following a long string of victories by Astaniran Democratic forces against isolationist forces, Qianxun had sufficiently strengthened itself against social fascist currents in global politics. However, the final triumph was not yet. For there to be a true, revolutionary, and classless society, there must be a people's struggle in every corner, in every city, in every desolate mountain top, and in every beach landing controlled by the social fascist international order. At the present time, the socialist parties aligned with the Min Zhu Party have endeavored greatly and endured painfully to preserve the ideals of the people's democratic revolution. However, these struggles have operated in isolation, with central committees and programs drawn up according to state lines, lines that must be blurred and dissolved.

Worse still, sinister forces now exist in Jomsland and Thyven and among the social fascist member states of the Elseyran Defense Union, who seek to undermine the just cause of global revolution. While none of the three leading New Socialist states would actually be affected by the recent asset seizures and economic sanctions imposed by these organizations, the need for global cooperation was nevertheless more urgent than ever in order to safeguard the proletariat from reactionary forces.

In a brief meeting of the Permanent Committee of the MZP Politburo, a consensus was reached at the insistence of general secretary Cui Fang to create a communist international of political parties to coordinate the global revolution everywhere. However, following explicit warnings from University staff such as Director-General Kang Hongxin and University party secretary Cui Jin, Cui acknowledged that hosting this international at Qianxun will draw unwanted attention from the other international socialist parties, who remain critical of its defense of market economics in the transition to socialism. Thus, after another meeting with Sanguinian officials at Ventusia, the decision was made to instead host this international instead at the coastal city of Citharo in Sanguivallis, historically a center of socialism during that country's first socialist era.

A provisional "conference of discussions" would be arranged with Astaniran and Sanguinian political parties on the exact composition of this new international, its official policy basis, scope, criteria for admission, and semantic rules. While officially the Renaissance Socialists under Pio Graci would be given seniority in the discussion, in practice the Qianxun parties under the MZP would dominate the drafting of the international's official statement of policies, incorporating several New Socialist frameworks such as vanguardism, the dictatorship of the proletariat, the two-stage theory, and a strict opposition to "social fascism" and traditional progressive politics.

Qianxun, Sanguivallis, and Astanir would be accorded "practical seats" in the international to reflect their position as governing parties closely aligned with Qianxun New Socialism, giving them seniority in the various committee assignments to be created for the international. Other delegates from Vespuria, Thyven, and Hydronia would be given "analytical seats" due to their speculative status as non-ruling or minor political entities in their respective countries. Other countries with major socialist currents like Lavia and Arenenge would be considered, though due to their strong independent policy bases, the MZP would persuade the conference of discussions against inviting them for fear of "diluting" the cause of international communism.

[b]Proclamation of the Socialist International[/b]

After finalizing its statement of policies, the Conference of Discussions would vote to dissolve itself on the 26th of February 2026. On the same day, the member parties of that conference would proclaim the establishment of the Socialist International during the First Conference of Discussions held at Citharo, in Sanguivallis. A total of 225 delegates in 22 party delegations from 8 nations would participate in this conference, the first time in the 21st century that such international coordination between socialist parties would be organized. The Presidium of the First Conference of Discussions would be organized according to the five major agendas set at that conference:

[list]

	Pio Graci (Sanguivallis), Chair of the Conference of Discussions

	Cui Fang (Qianxun), Vice-Chair on Admissions and Elections

	Rokan Gilon (Astanir), Vice-Chair on the Revolutionary Struggle

	Cui Jin (Qianxun), Vice-Chair on Propaganda

	Xenaro Sanjurjo (Thrysmora), Vice-Chair on the Liberal Question

	Argo Lo Pilato (Sanguivallis), Vice-Chair on Socialist Praxis

	Li Guowei (Qianxun), Central Administrator

[/list]

Formally, the Presidium was to act as the collective leadership of the First Conference of Discussions, though [i]de facto[/i] power would be concentrated in the hands of Cui Fang, who would be empowered by the Presidium to set the agenda on admission to the Socialist International, the election of its committees, and even the selection of new members to the Presidium itself, with Conference Chair Pio Graci largely being given a ceremonial role at the very top of the Presidium's order of precedence. Membership in this first Presidium would be dominated by members of the pro-Qianxun ruling communist parties, with Cui Fang promising the unrepresented parties membership in all future conferences.

On the participating parties and mass organizations, the composition of the Conference of Discussions' committee assignments would be expectedly dominated by the pro-Qianxun political parties under the strict supervision of the Min Zhu Party. Notable non-ruling communist parties and united fronts such as the Socialist Coalition of Vespurian and the Thrysmoran Socialist Workers' Party would figure prominently as theoreticians for discussions on armed struggle, while those represented in their national legislatures, like the Hydronic Workers' Party and the Yonwu Communist Party, would chiefly be designated with creating the orthodox praxis of the Socialist International. [b]Statement of Policies of the Socialist International[/b]

[list]

1. That the liberal-international order and the monarcho-fascist-international order are fundamentally unsustainable and must be utterly destroyed by a global, all-encompassing revolution of the proletariat.

2. That the protection of this global revolution can only be preserved through a dictatorship of the proletariat, which is to abolish the institutions and political frameworks of the liberal bourgeois, and institute in its place a participatory, multisectoral, and democratic government of the revolutionary vanguard.

3. That deviations from the dictatorship of the proletariat constitute a betrayal of the revolution and sanction of fascistic class collaboration.

4. That the final goal of every dictatorship is a stateless, classless, and communist society, which must be done appropriately in accordance with the transitional model from bourgeois capitalism to socialism, whereupon the productive mechanisms of the state are seized by the workers.

5. That the protracted people's war is the inevitable comrade of revolution and must be honorably prosecuted by the vanguard in close collaboration with the united front of the rural peasantry and the urban petite bourgeoisie.

6. That this protracted people's war must not include collaboration with centrist and right tendencies, who misuse the term "socialist" for their own gains, who empower liberal democratic institutions, and who encourage non-transitional class collaboration, disarm the revolution through gradualist placation of the masses.

7. That the Socialist International, founded upon this common platform for all representative socialist parties of the world, is empowered to coordinate and guide the revolution through the conferences of discussions and the proactive mandate of the socialist parties.

8. That this common platform be, at this time, be presented before the delegates of the Min Zhu Party, the Social-Radical Party, Qianxun Democratic Union, Xin Min Party, Qianxun Anti-Imperialist League, Constitutional Revolutionary Movement, Social Renaissance Party, Agrarian Party of Sanguivallis, the Astaniran Social Party, Astaniran National Party, Liberal Union, the "democratic", "new socialist" and "left tendecy" factions of the Socialist Coalition Party, the Left Currents of the Radical Party of Norrhollow under both Matthew Hultén and Samantha Gentzel, the Hydronic Workers' Party, 	the Yonwu Communist Party, Partido Socialista dos Trabalhadores, and the revolutionary student clubs of the Thyvenian academia.

[/list]

[b]Agendas of the First Conference of Discussions[/b]

[list]

[b]1. [i]Admissions and Elections[/i], by Cui Fang[/b]

[list]

[spoiler=Admissions and Elections]

a. All current and aspiring members of the Socialist International must be committed to the realization of a stateless, classless, and communist society. To seek the permanent preservation of the socialist state constitutes revisionism and opposition to the world revolution.

b. In countries with multiple participating political parties, they are to be represented in the Conferences of Discussions under a united front. If no such united front exists, or if there is only a single political party for that country, they shall be automatically identified simply as a "Section" of the Socialist International.

c. The protracted people's war is necessary where the revolution cannot be seamlessly executed. Those parties that reject this premise effectively sanction the dereliction of revolutionary duties even in the face of overwhelming imperialistic suppression.

d. The protracted people's war may be done legally through social agitation and propaganda to achieve immediate social demands, and illegally through armed struggle and the establishment of parallel governments. Deviations exist in the legal and illegal means of undertaking the protracted people's war, defined respectively as right and left opportunism. All member parties, therefore, must be able and willing to prosecute legal and illegal mechanisms to bring about the global revolution.

e. All centrist and reformist tendencies must be eradicated from all party leaderships to prevent the cause of revolution from being coopted by social fascism and class collaboration. Reformist programmes are to be supplanted by communist ones, approved by the Socialist International.

f. Member parties must regularly re-register their entire base, whether before each and every party congress or whenever expedient, to ensure the total loyalty of cadres to the socialist cause.

g. All member parties are required to publish their works in the [i]Acta Publica[/i], the official gazette of the Socialist International. Conversely, works of the Socialist International must be published in the official gazettes of each member party.

h. The Chair of the Conference of Discussions, the Vice-Chair on Admissions and Elections, and the Central Administrator are to be elected by the quorum of parties in the Conference proportional to their number of delegates. All other positions set for the agendas of the Conferences are to be elected by the quorum of parties, with each party obtaining exactly one vote.

i. Where it is expedient to assign the Presidium of the Conference of Discussions, the delegations of the Min Zhu Party of the Qianxun Socialist Republic and the Social Renaissance Party of the Sanguinian Democratic Republic may be automatically assigned to distribute positions by themselves.

[/spoiler]

[/list]

[b]2. [i]The Revolutionary Struggle[/i], by Rakon Gilon[/b]

[list]

[spoiler=The Revolutionary Struggle]

a. The war in Astanir is the first unambiguous and violent struggle of the 21st century between the proletariat revolution and fascist statism. It is the duty of all committed members of the Socialist International to recognize the legitimacy of the Democratic government of Chairman Horano Benir and to lend support to him, in whatever shape or form, until the final destruction of the Astaniran people's enemy.

b. The revolutionary struggle in Sanguivallis represents a version of the people's protracted war that has been chiefly driven by civilian, not military forces. Because of the speed of events, the Social Renaissance Party had no time to establish a parallel authority to the bourgeois government it sought to abolish, instead forcing it to adopt its institutions for itself. In all peaceful revolutionary struggles, this does not constitute immediate social fascism, and the revolutionary vanguard may continue to use bourgeois institutions so long as they are steadily supplanted by new state apparatuses dedicated to the emancipation of the proletariat, the seizure of the means of production, and the transition to a socialist economic model.

c. Within our ranks are parties currently facing repression and eradication in their own homelands, who have inherited a history of flagrant abuse by their imperialistic state apparatuses. It is the revolutionary duty of each member to support these parties, whether it be through direct intervention in their conflicts or provision of refuge during particularly grueling circumstances.

d. In such a nation where there is no revolutionary struggle, it is the duty of these member states to instigate one.

[/spoiler]

[/list]

[b]3. [i]Propaganda[/i], by Cui Jin[/b]

[list]

[spoiler=Propaganda]

a. The University of Qianxun Project 661 is an autonomous university within the wider University of Qianxun System. It operates under a collegiate system, with student bodies divided into a network of colleges operated by the Min Zhu Party, and halls of socialism operated by non-MZP bodies. We consider it to be the model education system for the integration of communist thought in all aspects of academic life.

b. The parties of the Socialist International are committed to expanding this form of socialist education to all echelons of academia. The ruling parties must endeavor to integrate socialist literature into their national curricula, while non-ruling parties must endeavor to do the same through alternative and parallel channels such as party schools and learning centers. These educational materials must meet a certain technical standard approved by the Standing Committee of the Presidium of the Socialist International.

c. What is known as "agitation" is committed directly by socialists upon the masses to build ground for revolution. These come in the form of rallies, petitions, armed struggles, phenomenological studies, anthropological studies, and other fieldwork. Agitation must be done cautiously and with the deputation of the International, lest it be destroyed through imperialistic overreaction.

d. What is known as "propaganda" is committed indirectly by socialists upon all sectors to dull the influence of the bourgeois state. These come in the form of humanistic pursuits in the arts, literature, music, and the dissemination of reports collated through direct agitation. Propaganda must be done liberally and with the guidance of the International to ensure that the proletariat is awakened and made militant in its support for its own liberation and self-actualization.

[/spoiler]

[/list]

a. The current socialist movement is beset by several errors that have hampered its ability to triumph over the imperialist institutions that rule over it. These errors come in three forms: theoretical, political, and organizational. Each of the three errors may be analyzed dialectically, with their theses, antitheses, and syntheses to confute and adjust their errors.

b. Theoretical errors come in two forms: revisionism and dogmatism. These two forces act as the undercurrents of all later errors. 

c. Revisionism constitutes social fascism. Since the dawn of the new millennium, all the nations of Erene have been dominated by two competing frameworks: that of the monarcho-fascist-international order and the liberal-international order. The monarcho-fascist-international abets socialist revisionism indirectly through the creation of popular fronts between revolutionaries seeking to establish a dictatorship of the proletariat and reactionaries merely seeking the elimination of monarcho-fascist forces to bring about the resumption of a bourgeois, liberal democratic political framework. The liberal-international order abets socialist revisionism directly, whereupon parties are systemically persuaded to abandon armed struggle in favor of a gradualist, parliamentarian approach to the people's democratic revolution that undermines all scientific understanding of the nature of capitalism. Today, wages have appreciated, and the standards of living all around Erene have increased, but this is not a permanent indication of the triumph of socialism but an example of its wanton, exploitative nature. In all capitalist countries, superficial growth is created by the corporations at the expense of the worker, financed through long budgetary deficits designed simply for the pursuit of the profit motive, and without any regard for the negative externalities that abound within. Capitalism, by its own nature, experiences highs and lows, driven by the natural reaction of socialized production against private appropriation. In Thyven, we have witnessed the eradication of the communist struggle through its systematic appropriation of parliamentarism and minimalism. These approaches have strengthened the powers of capitalism in Thyven and enabled its transition from the liberal-international order to the monarcho-fascist-international order. To participate in liberal democratic government is to pursue a legal avenue for revolutionary awakening, but to abandon all other means of attaining the revolution is to abandon its very purpose itself.

d. Dogmatism constitutes ideological paralysis. In all socialist parties, this is principally manifest through a rejection of the two prevailing schools of revolutionary thought in the 21st century: Dai Jun Thought and New Socialism. There can be no revolution in which revolutionaries refuse to account for the circumstances of their own national boundaries. Dogmatism in ruling parties throughout history, most notoriously in Sanguivallis during the Old Socialist era, was manifest through its overreliance on the urban petite bourgeoisie for the creation of an all-encompassing revolutionary vanguard. This halted the ability of Old Socialism to flourish in the country, with the rural peasantry of the country remaining foreigners to the intellectual sequence of events in the capital, who saw the mass and immediate collectivization of private property not as an emancipation of the proletariat but as theft by a bourgeois power masquerading as liberators. Without mass mobilization and popular support, the revolution existed within a fragile city ecosystem, undone soon after by reactionaries after performing the slightest military opposition. Dogmatism in non-ruling parties is marred by its overestimation of the people's power and underestimation of the state's power, in the creation of mass, regularized infantry formations aimed at immediately challenging the imperialist state in a series of optimistic and brazen military campaigns. Such misadventures go against the principles of the protracted people's war. Revolutionary struggle is all-encompassing, social, cultural, economic, and military, and must help to agitate the masses against the state apparatus. To do otherwise is to agitate the state against the people, who are left without any clear understanding of their place in the revolution. All members of the Socialist International must safeguard against ideological paralysis and study the two most important currents of socialism now present in our society: Dai Jun Thought to mobilize all sectors of society in the protracted people's war, and New Socialism to ensure the protection of the revolution after the inauguration of the people's dictatorship.

e. Political errors come in two forms: right and left opportunism, which are themselves variants of the theoretical errors. However, unlike theoretical errors, which fundamentally betray the socialist revolution by maligning its intellectual core, opportunism is an error in praxis alone. Theoretical errors prevent a revolution from ever manifesting in the first place, whereas opportunism diverts an incoming revolution in pursuit of short-sighted practical benefits.

f. Right opportunism underestimates the people's power and overestimates the state's power. Right opportunism is the praxic companion of revisionism and demarcates endeavors that directly weaken the people's protracted war through conciliation and compromise with imperialistic forces. Right opportunism concerns itself deeply with the well-being of the people and the good of the land, which seeks utilitarian solutions to erase immediate suffering, but does so at the cost of sacrificing the entire purpose of the revolution. No more was this right opportunism evident than in Qianxun itself, when revolutionary forces toppled the feudal Qianxun Empire, but then hesitated in instigating the fullest transition to a dictatorship of the proletariat for fear of political ostracization. Instead, believing that the salient objectives of the revolution had been achieved with the end of the monarchy and reasoning that the state needed to immediately impose law and order for the good of the land, right opportunists took over the ideological line of the revolution and installed a bourgeois liberal republic. This bourgeois liberal republic, known to us as the Qianxun Democratic Republic, was semi-feudal and semi-imperialistic, and so had to also be destroyed in the Battle of Danxia to pave the way for a true people's revolution.

g. Left opportunism overestimates the people's power and underestimates the state's power. Left opportunism is the praxic companion of dogmatism and demarcates endeavors that indirectly weaken the people's protracted war through misguided militancy, ill-equipped strategic counteroffensives, and a prevailing sense of belief in victory with the coming decisive battle. Perhaps the greatest example of this left opportunism in recent memory comes from the Arbeit-Sozialbund ("Labor-Social Bund"), a revolutionary but ultimately short-sighted union of militant laborers who sought in the 1920s to transform the prevailing leftist currents in Hochdeutsche politics at the time into a revolutionary wave against the imperial monarchy. Particularly in 1923, Bundist agitators under the leadership of co-chairmen Per Seydel and Franz Leopold von der Damerau instigated a controversial general strike and mass insurrection involving nearly 56% of all metal workers, 40% of public transportation workers, and a staggering 78% of sanitation workers, organized following rising heart and lung diseases within their respective industries. No more was this right opportunism evident than in Qianxun itself, when revolutionary forces toppled the feudal Qianxun Empire, but then hesitated in instigating the fullest transition to a dictatorship of the proletariat for fear of political ostracization. Instead, believing that the salient objectives of the revolution had been achieved with the end of the monarchy and reasoning that the state needed to immediately impose law and order for the good of the land, right opportunists took over the ideological line of the revolution and installed a bourgeois liberal republic. This bourgeois liberal republic, known to us as the Qianxun Democratic Republic, was semi-feudal and semi-imperialistic, and so had to also be destroyed in the Battle of Danxia to pave the way for a true people's revolution.

g. Left opportunism overestimates the people's power and underestimates the state's power. Left opportunism is the praxic companion of dogmatism and demarcates endeavors that indirectly weaken the people's protracted war through misguided militancy, ill-equipped strategic counteroffensives, and a prevailing sense of belief in victory with the coming decisive battle. Perhaps the greatest example of this left opportunism in recent memory comes from the Arbeit-Sozialbund ("Labor-Social Bund"), a revolutionary but ultimately short-sighted union of militant laborers who sought in the 1920s to transform the prevailing leftist currents in Hochdeutsche politics at the time into a revolutionary wave against the imperial monarchy. Particularly in 1923, Bundist agitators under the leadership of co-chairmen Per Seydel and Franz Leopold von der Damerau instigated a controversial general strike and mass insurrection involving nearly 56% of all metal workers, 40% of public transportation workers, and a staggering 78% of sanitation workers, organized following rising heart and lung diseases within their respective industries. The objectives of these concurrent strikes were deliberately inflammatory, with a list of objectives that were knowingly intolerable to the Kaiserreich's center-left parties. Having expected the support of the urban petite bourgeoisie, strikers were instead strategically fired and replaced by the Imperial government, while spontaneous risings were rigorously pursued and destroyed by the Imperial Army, who had sought a triumphant revolution without either the clear support of the people or sufficient armaments with which to sustain a protracted people's war.

h. Organizational error comes in two forms: dogmatic organization and revisionist organization. Dogmatic organization, as in the case of the Labor-Social Bund, limits the scale of its proliferation by prioritizing intellectual victories among the malleable urban petite bourgeosie, while the wider rural masses are left unengaged. Towards the end of the 1920s, Bundists made no attempt to expand their movement into a mass national character, with Bund cadres concentrated almost entirely in Neudresden, which acted as the lethargic seat of power of the Zentralrat. When these Bundists were then motivated by revolutionary fervor during the leftist surges, they lacked the appropriate party base to establish a proper dictatorship of the proletariat. Revisionist organization is the antithesis, constituted by wanton mergers of "like-minded" socialist parties without sufficiently educating new cadres in socialist orthodoxy. A vanguard party must maintain uncompromising iron discipline in both theory and praxis, as in the Old Socialist Coalition of High Albany, created as a popular front of liberals, democratic socialists, and communists solely as a leftist current against the status quo without any regard for ideological cohesion and quality assessments on party cadres. During the course of events, its party membership was gradually supplanted by the petite bourgeoisie, who pushed the OSC towards the right opportunist line, leading to mass departures and splinters. Bereft of both power and identity, all that remains of the OSC today is its legacy as the predecessor of the modern Socialist Coalition Parties of Vespuria. The vanguard must lead the revolution in conjunction with the radicalized masses. A national united front of all sectors must maintain ideological cohesion through rigorous re-registration and vetting of its cadres. To do otherwise is to disarm the vanguard of the revolution and lay it naked before the imperialist powers of the world.

i. For the world revolution to occur, the member parties of this Socialist International must first identify and confute the errors embedded within their political doctrines. Theoretical deviations must be eradicated to preserve the revolution, while opportunism should be reined in. Good socialist praxis is expected and shall be done.
